recent_violations.inspector_comments: THE RESIDENT OF THIS SINGLE FAMILY HOME WHO STATED AN EVENT SPACE HAS BEEN OPERATING IN HIS BASEMENT ON AN ONGOING BASIS (SOCIAL MEDIA SITES ADVERTIZED A RECENT 3 YEAR ANNIVERSERY EVENT) REFUSED TO ALLOW THIS BACP / DOB TASK FORCE TO CONDUCT A LICENSE / BUILDING INSPECTION. ALTHOUGH A REAR BASEMENT EXIT WAS OBSERVED ON THIS NIGHT, IT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED, DUE TO THE PROPRIETORS REFUSAL TO ALLOW A SAFETY INSPECTION, THAT THERE WAS A 2CD EXIT. THE SAFETY CONCERN IS IMMINENT IN NATURE BECAUSE SAID PROPRIETOR STATED THERE WERE 50 PEOPLE IN HIS UNLICENSED BASEMENT EVENT SPACE THAT NIGHT AND AT OTHER TIMES UP TO 100 ATTENDESS ARE IN THIS SINGLE FAMILY HOME BASEMENT EVENT SPACE. THIS PROPRIETOR ALSO REFUSED ENTRY TO ESTABLISH IF THERE WERE SMOKE DETECTORS, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS OR EXIT SIGNS.THIS SPACE, BASED ON THE PROPRIETORS REFUSAL TO ALLOW A SAFETY INSPECTION OF THIS UNLICENSED VENUE AND NUMEROUS SOCIAL MEDIA VIDEOS OBSERVED WHERE A 2CD EXIT CANNOT BEEN VERIFIED, MUST BE CONSIDERED DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS. BACP HAS ISSUED 3 CEASE AND DESIST ORDERS. IT IS IMPERATIVE DOB BE ALLOWED TO CONDUCT A SAFETY INSPECTION IN THE EVENT THE CEASE AND DESIST ORDERS ARE VIOLATED AND ANOTHER EVENT OCCURS.SECTION 14A-1-104.7 AND 14A-1-104.13.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS INSPECTION OCCURRED ON 8/28/2024 AT 6:30 PM. THIS 1 STORY SINGLE FAMILY HOME HAS BEEN OPERATING A PPA EVENT SPACE IN THE BASEMENT FOR THE PAST 3 YEARS WITH VARIOUS PERFORMERS THAT INCLUDE LIVE BANDS AND STAND UP COMEDIANS. THIS ILLEGAL EVENT SPACE IS ADVERTIZED ON ALL OF THE SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS AND HAS BOOKINGS WELL INTO 2025. ALTHOUGH THE TASK FORCE WAS REFUSED ENTRY, THE PROPRIETOR CLEARLY VERIFIED THIS ACTIVITY WAS INDEED HAPPENING INCLUDING THAT NIGHTS' EVENT. HE ALSO STATED THERE WERE APPROXIMATELY 50 PAID ATTENDEES AT THAT NIGHTS EVENT. HE CLAIMS THE COMPENSATION FOR ATTENDANCE IS IN THE FORM OF A "DONATION". DONATION NOTWITHSTANDING, MONEY IS EXCHANGED FROM THE ATTENDEES TO THIS PROPRIETOR FOR ENTRY TO THE VENUE VIA A VARIETY OF PAYMENT METHODS. BACP ISSUED CEASE AND DESIST ORDERS FOR THE FOOD SERVICE, ALCOHOL SERVICE AND UNLICENSED PPA ACTIVITY.VIDEOS OF DOZENS OF EVENTS CLEARLY SHOW THIS BASEMENT EVENT SPACE IN OPERATION. THIS PROPRIETOR REFUSED THIS TASK FORCE ENTRY DESPITE THE FACT THAT THE TASK FORCE WAS THERE TO CONDUCT A LEGITIMATE LICENSE INSPECTION BASED ON A COMPLAINT.PLANS AND PERMITS ARE REQUIRED AS PART OF THE MULTI-STAGE PPA LICENSE APPLICATION PROCESS. THERE IS NO EVIDENSE OF ANY APPLICATION FOR A PPA LICENSE ON FILE. THE PROPRIETOR RESIDES IN THIS SINGLE FAMILY HOME.THERE WERE NUMEROUS PEOPLE OUTSIDE OF THIS UNLICENSED BASMENT EVENT SPACE (IN THE BACK YARD). ALCOHOL AND FOOD WERE OBSERVED BEING CONSUMED BY THE EVENTS' ATTENDEES OUTSIDE. THERE WERE MORE ATTENDEES ARRIVING DURING THE COURSE OF THIS INSPECTION. A DOB CLOSURE ORDER FOR THIS UNLICENSED PPA EVENT SPACE IS UNDER CONSIDERATION PENDING A FULL INTERIOR INSPECTION.ALSO, THIS 1 STORY SINGLE FAMILY HOME HAS HAD AN ATTIC DOORMER INSTALLED ON THE EAST ROOF WITHOUT PLANS / PERMITS.NOTE; AS PART OF THE APPLICATION PROCESS FOR A PPA LICENSE A ZONING CERTIFICATION IS REQUIRED. THIS ZONING CERTIFICATE MUST CLEARLY INDICATE THE ALLOWANCE OF A PPA EVENT SPACE IN WHATEVER LOCATION THE APPLICANTS' PROPERTY IS LOCATED. IN THIS CASE, THIS SINGLE FAMILY HOME WITH AN UNLICENSED BASEMENT COMEDY CLUB / LIVE MUSIC VENUE THAT CHARGES MONEY FOR ADMISSION, SELLS FOOD AND ALCOHOL, CANNOT ACQUIRE THE PROPER LICENSE BASED ON THE FACT THAT THIS HOUSE AT 3514 W. POTOMAC IS ON A BLOCK OF RESIDENTIAL HOMES ZONED RS-3 (RESIDENTIAL ONLY).SECTION 14A-4-401.1

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
